title: 10 More and 10 Less Worksheets
intro: Show how adding or subtracting ten changes a number's groups.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Add or remove one tens rod while leaving the ones in place. Connect the action to the written result.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

10 less than 34 is 24.
10 more than 34 is 44.

Build 34 with three bundles of ten objects and four loose objects. Remove one bundle to show 24. Rebuild 34, then add one bundle to show 44.

Ask your student

What changed, and what stayed the same?

If your student needs help

If the student relies on a digit shortcut across a hundred, model the necessary regrouping.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each sheet contains three “ten more” and three “ten less” questions, alternating across six distinct prompts. Starting numbers range from 10 through 89, and answers range from 0 through 99. A set does not guarantee a zero answer or a starting number ending in zero.
